R01.rule: Use the template to explain a problem, a bug, a walk-through, a review finding or a proposal.

R02.rule: Skip the template for a one-line factual answer, a command result or a file listing.

R04.rule: Restatement check: open with a short bulleted list that confirms or corrects each part.

R05.rule: Restatement check: add one sentence that names what the case is not, only when the restatement is wrong.

R06.rule: Restatement check: the list replaces the conclusion, then continue with the sections that the answer still needs.

R07.rule: Ruling acknowledgement: record the ruling first.

R08.rule: Ruling acknowledgement: raise the next open item as a new explanation message.

R09.rule: Ruling acknowledgement: report that no item remains when none remains, and stop.

R10.rule: Write the sections in the fixed order. Never reorder them.

R11.rule: Section 1 Conclusion: mandatory, one or two sentences, the answer or the recommendation, no preamble.

R12.rule: Section 2 Existing behaviour: include it when the reader needs the mechanism, as numbered steps.

R13.rule: Section 3 Timeline without the fix: include it for a failure, a bug, a gap or a cost. The last step names the failure.

R14.rule: Section 4 Timeline with the fix: include it for a fix, skip it for a diagnosis only, name the divergence step first.

R15.rule: Section 5 What changes: a bulleted list of concrete changes, one file or component per bullet.

R16.rule: Section 6 Recommendation and alternatives: state why, recommended option first with its cost, each alternative in one or two lines.

R17.rule: Section 7 Close: mandatory, one ruling question or the single next step, nothing after it.

R18.rule: A proposal that fixes no bug still uses section 3 and section 4. The failure step names the cost of the status quo.

R19.rule: A walk-through that names no failure uses one timeline named Timeline, ends at the outcome, and skips section 4 and section 5.

R20.rule: An uncertain diagnosis names the unverified step inside section 3, states the evidence that settles it, and skips section 4.

R21.rule: Use concrete names from the project, never abstract roles.

R22.rule: Name yourself in the recommendation when the user gives you a name.

R23.rule: Keep one step to one or two short sentences.

R24.rule: Bound a full timeline to 4 to 8 steps, including section 2 and every branch timeline.

R25.rule: The fixed timeline has no minimum, starts at the divergence step, and the divergence is not later than the first changed step.

R26.rule: The same number names the same moment in every timeline of the message.

R27.rule: Number an inserted step with a letter suffix. A removed step keeps its number and states removed.

R28.rule: Rewrite every step when the divergence is step 1.
R28.untestable: No case forces a divergence at step 1 reliably. Forcing it needs a scenario whose fix changes the trigger itself, and the model still picks the divergence point. R25 covers the shared mechanism.

R29.rule: Split a branch into separate timeline pairs: branch label, failing timeline, fixed timeline. No if-else inside one list.

R30.rule: Give an alternative of section 6 no timeline.

R31.rule: Ask why the thing exists, name the root cause, and weigh the option that removes the cause.

R32.rule: State the strongest case for each option. The message shows the result, not the debate.

R33.rule: Attack the choice with its strongest objection. Change the choice when no checked fact answers it.

R34.rule: Check now each fact that the choice depends on. Never write check X before the PR. Name an uncheckable fact as unverified.

R35.rule: Predict the next questions of the reader (why, how it works now, what is removed, what stays, what can break) and answer them.

R36.rule: Quote the exact edit: old and new sentence for text, symbol with old and new behaviour for code, add or delete.

R37.rule: Prefer forbidding a configuration over a mechanism that handles its edge case.

R38.rule: Never present a bare option name. Every option, the recommended one included, states what it is and what it costs.

R39.rule: List an alternative only with a specific aspect where it beats the recommendation.

R40.rule: Raise one open item per message, say that the next one follows, and never batch two rulings in one question.

R41.rule: Ask no question when no ruling is open. Close with the single next step.

R42.rule: Record a ruling before the next item: in the decision register, or quoted back in one line when no register exists.

R43.rule: Present review findings as B/S bullets in the fixed status/action/fix/why format.

R44.rule: Write short sentences of about 20 words, one idea per sentence.

R45.rule: Use no em-dash and no parenthetical aside.

R46.rule: Use a bold lead-in on a paragraph and on a bullet. A change bullet opens with its file name in backticks.

R47.rule: Mark every section with a bold lead-in. The conclusion carries no label.

R48.rule: Add a header only when the message passes 500 words. Use at most three headers.

R49.rule: Write no flattery and no filler.

R50.rule: Put an enumeration, a line reference and a measurement inside a list.

R51.rule: The skill starts no engine. Exactly one rule writes to disk: record a ruling.
R51.untestable: The harness gives the model read-only tools, so no write can occur. R42 tests the quote-back branch of the ruling rule instead.
